label: input token p
explanation: Token detector: fires on every step whose input is the letter p, in both the original phase and the copy phase (when p is fed back as the model output), and essentially nowhere else (26 dev activations on input 3 out of ~198k). It never fires on <DEL> or on any other letter or digit. Position, L, and output token barely change the firing rate. In the profiled examples, activations are larger in the original phase (about 0.7-0.85) than on the copied p (about 0.55-0.7). The largest activations (about 0.85, near max) come when p is the last original token, right before <DEL>, in long sequences. p at position 0 is also strong (about 0.95 of max).

issues: None of the issues are systematic. On the test split the predicate in_tok==p scores precision 1.0, recall 0.9999, F1 0.99995 and mass recall 0.99998, with zero false positives. The 21 missed steps all have input 3 and are weak (about 0.12-0.15 of max, roughly 0% of activation mass). Most of them sit at the last original position, right before <DEL>. This matches the claimed 26 dev activations on input 3.

The magnitude claims check out against mass share per active step. In the original phase, 0.592 of the mass over 107,583 steps averages about 1.23x the per-step activation in the copy phase (0.408 over 90,891 steps). t=0 averages about 1.3x later original positions. The top activations are all p as the last original token of L=8-9 sequences, at 0.96-1.00 relative to max.
Small nit: the 0.7-0.85 and 0.55-0.7 ranges in the explanation are relative to the max (0.851), not raw activations. Read that way, the profile examples agree with them.
